- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early-to-mid horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates downside risk; increase early forecast lows and avoid sharp upward spikes.
- Model often overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00), especially in 30-day horizon — cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 20% below true outcome if sentiment is neutral.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts — if model shows >2.0x recent high or <0.5x recent low, adjust toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- Sentiment volatility (alternating +/–) correlates with model overfitting — dampen forecast variance in such periods; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 0.7x positive, 0.3x negative).
- If sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, model underperforms — add 0.1–0.3 to forecast lows to account for hidden risk.
- For 30d horizon, avoid extreme outliers (>10% above/below 10-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports them — use sentiment as a filter for outlier rejection.
